Subject: MSA kickoff — template decision log & security milestones

Hi Elena / Miguel —

Thanks for sending over the initial MSA. To make the intake efficient on our side, I attached a short party sheet and a decision-log template (party_sheet_avalon.xlsx and a blank decision log) so we can capture decisions as we go. Two asks to get us moving: 

1) Please confirm the contracting counterparty name and billing address you want on the MSA (legal entity, tax ID if available).
2) Can you flag any non-standard clauses you expect (e.g., data residency carve-outs, custom IP language, audit rights) so we can prioritize redlines?

On security: our SOC2 checklist is standard for new enterprise customers. If you can provide an estimated delivery date for any requested evidence (infrastructure diagrams, SOC2 report, or a self-attestation), we can map milestones and avoid blocking the Professional Services kickoff.

Proposed short timeline:
- Today: capture counterparty + scope items in the party sheet
- Wed (6/11): legal/technical sync if you have outstanding security asks
- Fri (6/13): redline pass (first pass) from Redwood legal

Kimberly (cc’d) will lead the redline intake on our side — Kim, anything to add on our internal timeline?

Thanks,
Avery

--
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

- Counterparty: Avalon Works, Inc.
- Billing address: 220 Marin St, Suite 400, San Rafael, CA 94901

Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA kickoff — template decision log & security milestones

Thanks — looping in a lightweight intake checklist so our legal intake is reproducible. Quick notes/focus areas (I’ll attach highlights as comments in our first-pass redline):

- Counterparty verification: once party_sheet_avalon.xlsx is returned we’ll confirm signing authority / signatory matrix.
- IP: if Avalon requests an IP carve-out for PS deliverables, please flag whether the language should be limited (e.g., license back for product integration) vs assignment. That materially changes negotiation posture.
- Data residency: if EU PII is in scope we will propose conditional data residency language and clarify where Redwood hosts production data for Avalon.
- Liability / caps: expect our standard cap language; if Avalon needs a higher cap for enterprise procurement, we’ll document the business case for leadership approval.
- Security evidence: Miguel — once you share SOC2 and infra diagram, we’ll run the security triage and confirm if MSA requires an attachment (exhibit) for security controls.

Proposed next steps:
1) Avalon returns the filled party sheet (today).
2) Miguel uploads SOC2 PDF + infra diagram to the Drive link (Thu 6/12).
3) Redwood legal returns first-pass redline (Fri 6/13) with inline comments and a short decision log.

I’ve attached a one-page redline intake checklist for your procurement team (short checklist). If there are any hard stop dates for your procurement/PO process, please share so we can align review cadence.

Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: redline_intake_checklist.pdf

Subject: Re: MSA kickoff — template decision log & security milestones

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Elena / Miguel.

Thanks for confirming the counterparty and the timeline for SOC2 — that aligns with our internal plan. Two quick organizational items:

- I scheduled a 30-minute sync for Thu 6/12 11:00am PT (calendar invite sent) to walk through the party sheet and security attachments. If that doesn’t work for your team, propose an alternate time.
- I uploaded a shared decision-log to the Drive folder linked above; please add any proposed non-standard language so we can capture tradeoffs and approvals while redlining.

Kim — once you have the first-pass redline, can you add a short summary of the material items in the decision log so our CS/PS teams can scope kickoff dependencies?

If all goes to plan we’ll aim for PO issuance by mid-July. Thanks team — talk soon.

Avery
